papers.title: Temperature modulates sexual reproduction in a globally invasive plant species via self‐fertilisation
papers.recommendationReason: 重点体现前沿突破；命中“mechanism”等信号。

essence.problem: Abstract Sexual reproduction is critical for the success of plant invasion, but is constrained in novel environments by mate availability and temperature.
essence.design: Here, we conducted four field surveys over a 10‐year period and 2‐year pollination experiments in low‐ and high‐latitude greenhouse common gardens to determine whether there were evolutionary shifts in self‐incompatibility and to identify the latitudinal cline of self‐fertilisation.
